messages:
sara: FYI saw partial KMS degradation in us-west last night, some jump-hosts fell back to local keystore but we didn't have ephemeral RBAC in place. Drafting a short mitigation + post-incident checklist.

kevin: ugh. can you outline the minimum privileges we need? don’t want to open cluster roles to the ops team.

anna: minimal approach: create dedicated SA in jump-hosts namespace + Role with keystore.read, keystore.write, and secrets.update. RoleBinding should be ephemeral (TTL). No clusterRole.

mike: timeline for staging test? i'll own the canary if it's scripted. also: who handles audit exports for SOC?

ops-bot: System: KMS degradation detected 2026-03-22T23:12Z -> 2026-03-22T23:19Z (us-west-2). Error rate spike: 503s.

sara: plan in short: 1) create SA fallback-ops in jump-hosts, 2) apply Role + ephemeral RoleBinding (60m), 3) mount local-keystore secret on jumphosts, 4) enable keystore audit plugin + kube-audit verbose for canary, 5) run 2-host canary, 6) rotate fallback keys and revoke after success.

ellie: put runbook link when ready and add SOC correlation steps (request IDs, auth.Subject, host identity).

kevin: for auditing, export both audit logs and keystore plugin logs to secure S3 (s3://redwood-soc-archives/kms-incidents/) with 90d retention. ensure logs include `authenticator` and `imposter_check` fields.

anna: sketch of ephemeral binding (to be pushed via gitops):
```
# create service account
kubectl -n jump-hosts create sa fallback-ops
# create role with minimal verbs
kubectl -n jump-hosts apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: Role
metadata:
  name: keystore-operator
rules:
- apiGroups: ["keystore.redwood.io"]
  resources: ["keys","keystoreconfigs"]
  verbs: ["get","list","watch","update","patch"]
EOF
# ephemeral binding created via controller or one-shot Job that deletes after TTL
```

kevin: Q: do we need to rotate local fallback keys after a failover? compliance probably wants rotation and attestation.

sara: yes rotate immediately after we validate canary. add step to push revocations to any cached clients and to update cosign attestations for any images changed.

mike: note for canary: add backoff so jumphost doesn't rapidly flip between KMS and local keystore. config snippet: `RETRY_BACKOFF_MS=200, RETRY_MAX=6`. also emit metric: `keystore.fallback.count` and `keystore.fallback.latency_ms`.

ellie: i'll add SOC alert rules: pager if `keystore.fallback.count > 5` within 5m and create dashboard tile with fallback hosts + last-auth-actor.

anna: small compliance note: when creating ephemeral RoleBinding, include annotation `created-by: runbook/operator-name` and require operator to run with `kubectl --record` so we can trace who executed it. add example commit message template in runbook.

sara: pushed a draft runbook to https://internal.redwood/sops/runbooks/keystore-ephemeral-fallback (draft). pasted quick test commands below.

sara: ```bash
# apply local fallback secret on host
kubectl -n jump-hosts create secret generic local-keystore --from-file=keystore.json=./keystore.json --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
# patch deployment to enable fallback
kubectl -n jump-hosts set env daemon/jumphost FALLBACK_KS=local --record
# create RoleBinding via gitops PR (example snippet attached in runbook)
```

kevin: good. after canary, export audit slice: `kubectl logs -n kube-system kube-audit-collector --since-time=\"2026-03-22T23:00:00Z\" | gzip > audit-slice.gz` then upload to s3 with server-side encryption. I'll own that.

mike: i can run canary tomorrow 09:30 PT (1749991800-ish). anna, can you finish the binding script and QA it in dev?

anna: will write the binding controller prototype (deletes binding after TTL) and open PR against infra-gitops. PR template will include operator name, reason, and TTL.

ellie: SOC will need correlation keys: request_id, host_instance_id, service_account, and cosign signature IDs if images are touched. Add those fields to runbook output.

ops-bot: Reminder: open incident ticket INC-2026-03122 and tag #security #infra #soc.

sara: assigning owners in runbook: anna -> binding script & PR, mike -> canary run, kevin -> audit export + S3 upload, ellie -> SOC triage + artifacts. i'll own runbook edits and postmortem.

mike: last thing 1: if fallback keys are used, we should enforce an immediate TTLed denylist for any tokens that were minted with local creds. add revoke step to runbook.

anna: noted, will add revoke API calls and cosign re-attestation checklist.

kevin: once postmortem is ready, include a timeline, root cause, and a list of short-lived mitigations vs long-term fixes (e.g., resilient KMS SDK, client-side caching with proof-of-authority).

ellie: i'll collate artifacts after canary and run SOC correlation. send any log snippets to `#security-evidence` channel.

sara: thanks everyone. i'll roll this into the final runbook and request the gitops PRs. closing thread once PRs are merged.
